newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle first quarter sales rise 18.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nestle first quarter sales rise 18.7 pct.

text.p: Swiss food and beverage group Nestle SA said on Tuesday group sales had risen 18.7 percent in the first quarter to 16.1 billion Swiss francs and it expected good growth in sales and profits in the current year.
"The preliminary April figures confirm this trend," Nestle said in a statement released at its annual news conference.
Most of the sales increase, however, came from favourable exchange rates and the growth rate is likely to ease during the second half of the year, Nestle added.
In the first quarter sales volume grew 2.2 percent.
The stock market reacted with disappointment to Nestle's results, pushing down the share by almost one percent to 1,820 francs shortly after the results were announced.
The market had generally been looking for a rise in first quarter sales of around 20 percent compared with the reported 18.7 percent, dealers said.

"Nestle expects good growth in both consolidated sales and consolidated net profit for the whole of the year. It is clear, however, that the rhythm of growth will diminish in the course of the second semester, since the foreign exchange comparison will be established on a less favourable base," Nestle said.

Net monetary factors accounted for 15.7 percent of the first quarter sales rise with selling price increases and other factors accounted for 2.7 percentage points and variation of exchange rates was 13.0 points.
The net effect of acquisitions and disposals was 0.2 percentage points.

Among the major currencies, the dollar's weighted average exchange rose 21.0 percent against the Swiss franc in the first quarter from the first quarter of 1996. The French franc rose 8.9 percent, the German mark 6.9 percent and British sterling 28.6 percent.
In 1996 Nestle's sales grew 7.1 percent to 60.49 billion francs and net profit rose 16.6 percent to 3.40 billion francs.
